label: MiniMax M3.1 Flash
output:
Here's your reply, written calm and plain, with the facts, the offer still open, and no fighting:

---

**Renee,**

First — I'm sorry. I truly am sorry your toe hurt, and I'm sorry this was a frightening thing to go through. A red, hot, swollen toe is miserable, and I would have felt the same way you did. Nobody in my family has been through what you went through, and I take infections seriously. I'm not writing to argue with you, and I'm not writing to blame you either. You were the one in pain.

I'm the owner of Lotus Garden Nails, so let me tell you what actually happened on Oct 24, because some of it isn't what I heard you say.

You had a deluxe pedicure, $45. The tech was my niece, Vy. She's been licensed three years, she was born in Houston, and she speaks English just fine — she's quiet and shy, that's all. She's not someone who rushes, and she will always tell you when something needs to be gentler.

That day you asked her to keep working on the cuticle. You asked for more, more, and you told her it was fine because you always do it that way. Vy did tell you it was too much. I know that part hurts to hear, and my family owns it. But I want you to know the choice was yours, and she did try to slow it down.

On the cleanliness side, I know that's the part that scares people the most, so please believe me:

- Every tool comes out of the autoclave in a sealed pouch, and we open it in front of you
- Your file and buffer were brand new, and you took them home
- The tub gets a fresh plastic liner every time, for every customer
- We passed our state inspection in August 2026 with no violations. The certificate is on the wall. You've already filed with the state, and we will cooperate with anything they ask of us — we're not afraid of that.

When you came back on Nov 2 and showed me the toe, I apologized to you in person and offered you your full $45 back, plus payment of your urgent care copay if you bring me the receipt. **That offer is still open.** You asked for $300 cash and a year of free pedicures, and I couldn't agree to that. I hope you understand I said no because that isn't something I was able to promise — not because I didn't care about your toe.

What hurt me most was reading that all these places are dirty, like we are all the same. My family has done this in Houston for 19 years. We opened in 2007, right after I finished working for my aunt. In all that time I have never had one infection complaint. If we had been cutting corners, I would take full responsibility in a heartbeat, and I would fix it.

I'll say this gently: when Vy read your post, she cried all night and told me she wanted to leave the business. She's a good tech who genuinely cares about people. I would ask you to think about that before saying again that she barely speaks English or couldn't do the job.

Marisol, thank you for the kind words, and thank you for suggesting she talk to the owner. You're right — that's the best thing she could do.

Renee, please call the salon and ask for me, or just come in. My number is on the salon phone and I'll be there every day. I would much rather sit down with you, hear exactly what happened, and make it right than argue with you on a forum. You are still welcome here — and so is anyone else who read this and was worried about us.

— Owner, Lotus Garden Nails, Bellaire
